```{python}
#| label: fig-bench-kv-contains
#| fig-cap: "Contains key latency across three scales: CoordKV2 (flat) vs HashMap (bool advantage erased by cache pressure)"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

scales = ['10k', '1M', '10M']
x = np.arange(len(scales))

kv2 = [21.7, 21.6, 21.6]
hm  = [13.0, 19.9, 19.9]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.5, 3.5))

ax.plot(x, kv2, '-o', color='black', markerfacecolor='white', markeredgecolor='black',
        markersize=8, linewidth=1.8, label='CoordKV2 (dense array)')
ax.plot(x, hm, '-s', color='black', markerfacecolor='black', markeredgecolor='black',
        markersize=8, linewidth=1.8, label='HashMap (SipHash + bucket)')

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels([f'{s}\nops' for s in scales], fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel('Per-op latency (ns)', fontsize=10)
ax.set_ylim(8, 28)
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper left')
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle=':', alpha=0.4)

# Value labels
for xi, y1, y2 in zip(x, kv2, hm):
    ax.text(xi - 0.1, y1 + 1.0, f'{y1} ns', fontsize=8, ha='center')
    ax.text(xi + 0.1, y2 + 1.0, f'{y2} ns', fontsize=8, ha='center')



plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```
